IT DOES NOT WRITE content_items: title/content/excerpt/meta_title/meta_description/meta_keywords land in the VERSION only, so passing edited values returns 201 while the live item is untouched a…

tools.name: content_versions_list
tools.description: Page through the saved snapshots of a marketing content item, newest version_number first. Returns {data:[{id, version_number, title, content, excerpt, meta_title, meta_description, meta_keywords, change_summary, created_by, created_at}], pagination:{page, limit, total, total_pages}}, or 404 'Content item not found' when the id is not in this account. Unlike content_get, which embeds only the late…

tools.name: create_task
tools.description: Create a new PM task with title, description, priority, type, assignee, and due date. Field is `title` (NOT `name` — that's the pm_projects field). The route also accepts `name` as a forgiving alias if you forget. Prefer pm_tasks_create going forward; this name is kept for backwards compatibility.

tools.name: crm_account_summary
tools.description: High-level account snapshot: contact/company/deal/pipeline counts, active sequences, suppressions, open-deal $ total. Cheap; use as a first read when the user asks "give me an overview." Contacts, companies and deals count LIVE rows only (soft-deleted rows excluded), the same basis as crm_contact_list and account_audit_health.crm.contact_count, so those three totals are directly comparable. `count…

tools.name: crm_activity_leaderboard
tools.description: Activity counts per user (calls/emails/meetings/tasks logged) over a rolling window. Default 30 days.

tools.name: crm_add_lead_source_option
tools.description: Add a custom lead-source option (or un-archive an existing slug).

tools.name: crm_add_lead_status_option
tools.description: Add a custom lead-status option (or un-archive an existing slug). System slugs are reserved.

tools.name: crm_archive_lead_source_option
tools.description: Soft-archive a custom lead-source option. Default sources can't be archived.

tools.name: crm_archive_lead_status_option
tools.description: Soft-archive a custom lead-status option. System rows can't be archived. Existing contacts using this status keep their value.

tools.name: crm_attach_tag
tools.description: Attach a tag to a contact/company/deal. Idempotent — calling twice is safe. Tag scope (object_type on the tag row) is enforced; an account-wide tag (null object_type) attaches to any type.

tools.name: crm_audit_summary
tools.description: Aggregate CRM data-quality audit — the counts behind 'what is wrong with this CRM': missing emails, duplicate contacts, orphaned records and similar. Read-only; run before a cleanup so you act on numbers rather than impressions.

tools.name: crm_calendar_create
tools.description: Create a calendar event. attendees is a list of email addresses; conference=true adds a Google Meet / Microsoft Teams link.

tools.name: crm_calendar_delete
tools.description: Delete a calendar event.

tools.name: crm_calendar_get
tools.description: Fetch one calendar event with full detail (attendees, conference link).

tools.name: crm_calendar_list
tools.description: List upcoming/past calendar events (Google Calendar / Microsoft Graph via the account's connected OAuth). Optional time window + search.

tools.name: crm_calendar_update
tools.description: Update a calendar event (only the fields you pass are changed).

tools.name: crm_calls_list
tools.description: Call activities with recording and transcript detail. Filter by contact_id, company_id, deal_id, has_recording, has_transcript or a free-text search. This is the call history behind a contact — crm_get_contact does not include it.

tools.name: crm_companies_bulk_create
tools.description: Bulk-import companies. Up to 5,000 rows. Dedup precedence: external_id (if provided), then lowercase(name) within the account. Supports the same inline custom_fields + auto_create_fields contract as crm_contacts_bulk_create. Returns the same result shape.

tools.name: crm_contact_engagement_summary
tools.description: Single-call engagement snapshot for one contact: emails sent/received, opens/clicks, meetings/calls/notes/tasks, last-inbound/outbound timestamps, ratios, active-sequence list. Read-only.

tools.name: crm_contact_merge
tools.description: Merge loser_id INTO winner_id. Reparents activities, deal_contacts, contact_companies, tags, custom_field_values, sequence_enrollments, email_events, and suppressions. Backfills any blank winner field from the loser ("winner wins, loser fills blanks"). Soft-deletes the loser. Single transaction; partial failures don't leave the loser half-merged. DESTRUCTIVE — confirm with the rep before calling. …

tools.name: crm_contact_score_compute
tools.description: Recompute + persist a contact's lead_score from the last 30 days of engagement. Writes lead_score, lead_score_reason, lead_score_updated_at. Returns the new score (0-100), a reason summary, and the full component breakdown. Same weights as the sales DAO.

tools.name: crm_contact_status_option_create
tools.description: Add a lead-status option (value + label + colour) for the account. Use when a pipeline needs a stage the six defaults do not cover.

tools.name: crm_contact_status_options_list
tools.description: Lead-status options for the account. Seeds six system defaults on first call, so every account has a working baseline. Pass include_archived to see retired options too — useful when a contact carries a status no longer offered.

tools.name: crm_contact_touch_history
tools.description: Chronological merged timeline of activities + sequence email events for a contact. Sorted newest-first, capped at `limit` items across both sources combined.

tools.name: crm_contact_upsert_by_email
tools.description: Idempotent single-contact write keyed on lowercase(email). If a contact with that email exists in the account it's updated (only the fields you pass — existing values are preserved); otherwise it's created with lead_source='upsert'. Use for incremental re-imports + agent flows where you can't tell in advance whether the email is new. Supports inline custom_fields + auto_create_fields like the bulk…

tools.name: crm_contacts_bulk_create
tools.description: Bulk-import contacts into the CRM. Up to 5,000 rows per call; emails are normalized to lowercase before insert and the (account_id, email) unique index prevents duplicates at the DB level. Custom fields can be set inline via per-row `custom_fields: {key: value}`. With `auto_create_fields: true`, unknown field_keys auto-create the crm_custom_fields definition with type inferred from the first value…

tools.name: crm_contacts_duplicates
tools.description: Find duplicate-candidate contacts grouped by lowercased email. Name-only matching is intentionally excluded (too many false positives). Returns groups with 2+ contacts each.

tools.name: crm_contacts_gone_cold
tools.description: Contacts who had engagement signals in the last 180 days then went silent for `days` days. Distinct from crm_contacts_stale (which catches "no activity ever"). Highest-ROI re-engagement bucket.

tools.name: crm_contacts_missing_field
tools.description: Contacts missing a standard column value. Use for data-quality sweeps ("which contacts have no phone?"). Valid fields: email, phone, first_name, last_name, job_title, lead_source, owner_id, assigned_to_id, lead_status.

tools.name: crm_contacts_stale
tools.description: Contacts with no recent crm_activities entry. Filters contacts where the latest activity is older than `days` (default 30) OR there are no activities at all.

tools.name: crm_contacts_top_scored
tools.description: Top N contacts by lead_score. Optional lifecycle_stage filter so "hottest leads" works without post-filtering. Excludes contacts whose score has never been computed.

tools.name: crm_contract_template_create
tools.description: Create a contract template. Provide EITHER layout_json (block-based, compiled to HTML server-side) OR source_pdf_s3_key + fields[] (legacy PDF + coordinate fields). signers[] is the role skeleton (e.g. [{role: "Client"}, {role: "Agency"}]).

tools.name: crm_contract_template_delete
tools.description: Archive a contract template (sets is_archived=true). Templates are never hard-deleted — historical envelopes still reference them for audit.

tools.name: crm_contract_template_get
tools.description: Get a single contract template by UUID. Returns layout_json + compiled_html (block path) or source_pdf_s3_key + fields_json (PDF path).

tools.name: crm_contract_template_list
tools.description: List contract templates. By default only non-archived templates are returned; pass archived=true to include archived ones.

tools.name: crm_contract_template_update
tools.description: Update a contract template. Only name, description, and is_archived are mutable here — to change the document body, create a new template (existing envelopes reference the template id for audit).

tools.name: crm_create_activity
tools.description: Log a CRM activity (note, call, email, meeting, or task) linked to a contact, company, or deal

tools.name: crm_create_company
tools.description: Create a new CRM company

tools.name: crm_create_contact
tools.description: Create a new CRM contact with name, email, phone, job title, lifecycle stage, optional company link, and OWNER. owner_id/assigned_to_id are public_users UUIDs validated against your account — pass owner_id to set the rep who owns the lead (assigned_to_id defaults to it). Without owner_id the contact is created unowned (null owner). Use crm_list_users / the account roster to resolve the rep UUID; d…

tools.name: crm_create_custom_field
tools.description: Define a new custom field on contact/company/deal/etc. field_key must be lowercase alphanumeric + underscore. After creating, write values via crm_set_custom_field_value.

tools.name: crm_create_deal
tools.description: Create a new CRM deal in a pipeline stage with optional value, contact, and company

tools.name: crm_create_email_template
tools.description: Create a new email template. Templates created via Olympus default to is_shared=true (visible account-wide) since service-key callers have no human user. Body/subject support merge tags with fallback syntax ({{first_name|there}}) and spintax for per-recipient variation ({Hi|Hey|Hello}) — see field descriptions.

tools.name: crm_create_pipeline
tools.description: Create a new CRM pipeline with optional stages

tools.name: crm_deals_at_risk
tools.description: Open deals exhibiting risk signals: stuck in current stage ≥ stuck_days (default 14) OR past their close_date. Returns risk_flags per deal so the agent can prioritize.

tools.name: crm_deals_bulk_create
tools.description: Bulk-import deals. Up to 5,000 rows. Dedup by external_id ONLY — deals don't have a natural uniqueness key. Pipeline + stage are required per-row OR via default_pipeline_id / default_stage_id (both are batch-validated against the account before any insert; mismatches fail fast for the whole batch). Optional contact_id / company_id per row creates the deal↔contact / deal↔company join rows. Same cus…

tools.name: crm_deals_stuck
tools.description: Open deals whose updated_at is older than `days` (default 14). Simpler than crm_deals_at_risk — pure stuck filter without close_date overlay.

tools.name: crm_delete_activity
tools.description: Delete a CRM activity by ID

tools.name: crm_delete_company
tools.description: Delete a CRM company by ID

tools.name: crm_delete_contact
tools.description: Delete a CRM contact by ID

tools.name: crm_delete_custom_field
tools.description: Hard-delete a custom field DEFINITION. Cascades the field's value rows on every object. Destructive — use rarely.

tools.name: crm_delete_deal
tools.description: Delete a CRM deal by ID

tools.name: crm_delete_email_template
tools.description: Soft-delete a template (sets archived_at). In-flight sequence enrollments that reference it still resolve at send time.

tools.name: crm_delete_sequence
tools.description: Hard-delete a sequence — cascades steps and enrollments. Use sparingly. Prefer is_active=false via crm_update_sequence for "stop using this" cases; delete only when truly removing.

tools.name: crm_delete_tag
tools.description: Delete a tag definition. Cascades crm_object_tags (every attachment is removed).

tools.name: crm_detach_tag
tools.description: Detach a tag from an object. No-op when not attached.

tools.name: crm_email_batch_cancel
tools.description: Cancel all queued rows in a batch (already-sent rows are untouched).

tools.name: crm_email_batch_reschedule
tools.description: Shift the fire time of a batch (all rows in the batch that are still queued).

tools.name: crm_email_send_queue_list
tools.description: List scheduled / sent / cancelled email send-queue rows. Filter by status, batch_id, or contact_id.

tools.name: crm_email_thread_search
tools.description: Search CRM-stored email activities (synced via crm_activities) by subject or body substring. Distinct from crm_ghl_contacts_search / crm_hubspot_contacts_search which hit the external CRM live.

tools.name: crm_enroll_sequence
tools.description: Enroll a contact in a sequence. The sequence must be is_active=true; if it is not, the API returns 400 "Sequence is not active" — check active state via crm_get_sequence first. Returns 409 with duplicate=true if the contact is already enrolled.

tools.name: crm_envelope_add_signer
tools.description: Append a signer to a draft envelope. Refuses (409) if envelope is not draft. Returns the new signer row plus the plaintext access token (not derivable from the stored hash — store it if you need to email a manual link). Signing order is auto-assigned to max+1.

tools.name: crm_envelope_create
tools.description: Create a draft envelope. Provide EITHER layout_json (block-based proposal — compiled server-side to HTML) OR source_pdf_s3_key + fields[] (legacy PDF + coordinate fields). signers[] is required (1-10). The response includes plaintext signer tokens — capture them; they are not derivable from the stored hash. signing_order = parallel | sequential.

tools.name: crm_envelope_delete
tools.description: Soft-delete an envelope (moves status to voided, sets deleted_at). Refuses (409) on completed envelopes — those are immutable for audit reasons.

tools.name: crm_envelope_get
tools.description: Get a single envelope by UUID, including signers, fields, recent events (last 100), and the full CRM linkage: contact (id, name, email, phone), company (id, name), and deal (id, name, value, stage). Response includes an ETag header reflecting updated_at for optimistic-concurrency PATCH.

tools.name: crm_envelope_list
tools.description: List signature envelopes (contracts/proposals). Filter by status (draft/sent/viewed/completed/declined/voided/all), contact_id, company_id, deal_id, or subject_type (estimate/contract/invoice/custom). limit defaults to 50, max 200. Each row includes signers, the linked contact (id, name, email), company (id, name), and deal (id, name, value, stage) so the agent has full CRM context in one call.

tools.name: crm_envelope_list_signers
tools.description: List signers on an envelope. Token hashes are NOT returned — only metadata (status, signed_at, viewed_at, reminder_count, etc.). Use this to check progress on a sent envelope without pulling the full envelope detail.

tools.name: crm_envelope_send
tools.description: Send signer-invitation emails. On first send, status moves draft → sent and per-signer plaintext access tokens are minted server-side. For parallel envelopes every pending signer is emailed; for sequential, only the first pending signer (downstream invites trigger on prior signer completion via the public sign route). Requires the from_email setting on crm_payment_integrations.

tools.name: crm_envelope_update
tools.description: PATCH a draft envelope. Refuses (409) if status != draft. Passing signers replaces the roster but preserves access tokens for signers identified by id. Pass an If-Match header equal to the previous ETag to detect concurrent edits (412 on mismatch). Use contact_id / company_id / deal_id to (re)link the envelope to CRM records — pass null to clear an existing link.

tools.name: crm_envelope_void
tools.description: Void an envelope (status → voided, stamps voided_at and void_reason). Refuses (409) on completed envelopes.

tools.name: crm_estimate_convert_to_invoice
tools.description: Convert an accepted estimate into a fresh draft invoice. Copies line items, totals, notes, and terms; links the invoice back via converted_invoice_id on the estimate; status moves to "converted"; portal tokens are revoked. Returns 409 if already converted.

tools.name: crm_estimate_create
tools.description: Create a draft estimate. Either contact_id OR company_id is required. line_items is an array of { description, quantity, unit_cents, discount_cents?, tax_bps?, sort_order?, product_id?, metadata? }. estimate_number is auto-generated server-side via the atomic doc-number helper.

tools.name: crm_estimate_delete
tools.description: Soft-delete an estimate and revoke its portal tokens. Refuses (409) on accepted/converted estimates — those are immutable for audit reasons.

tools.name: crm_estimate_get
tools.description: Get a single estimate by UUID, including line_items, contact, company, and deal.

tools.name: crm_estimate_list
tools.description: List CRM estimates with optional filters: status (draft/sent/viewed/accepted/declined/expired/converted/all), contact_id, company_id, deal_id, free-text q (matches estimate_number/notes/contact name/email/company name), order (created_desc/created_asc/expires_asc/expires_desc/total_desc/total_asc), pagination via limit/offset. Each row includes the linked contact, company, and deal (id, name, valu…

tools.name: crm_estimate_mark_accepted
tools.description: Record operator-side acceptance for an estimate (customer agreed verbally / over email and you're recording it). Stamps accepted_offline=true on the row and renders the acceptance certificate PDF. signer_name is the name the customer agreed under (e.g. "Jane Smith"). Returns 409 if the estimate is declined/expired. Idempotent on accepted/converted — replays return already_accepted=true.

tools.name: crm_estimate_send
tools.description: Send the estimate to the contact via email and/or SMS. Mints a single portal token (TTL 30d) shared across channels. channel = email | sms | both. Pass attach_pdf=true to render and attach the PDF on the email (text + portal link are sufficient otherwise). idempotency_key dedupes accidental re-sends. SMS branch requires the voice add-on enabled on the account.

tools.name: crm_estimate_template_create
tools.description: Create an estimate template. line_items is optional (a design-only template is valid); amount_cents is stamped server-side on each item. design_json is the customizable PDF design (theme/columns/sections/labels) applied when an estimate from this template is rendered. is_default=true makes it the account default (applied to blank estimates) and unsets any other default.

tools.name: crm_estimate_template_delete
tools.description: Soft-delete an estimate template (deleted_at timestamp; not surfaced in list).

tools.name: crm_estimate_template_get
tools.description: Get a single estimate template by UUID.

tools.name: crm_estimate_template_list
tools.description: List reusable estimate templates (name, description, currency, default tax, line items skeleton).

tools.name: crm_estimate_template_update
tools.description: Update an estimate template. Passing line_items replaces the full set. design_json replaces the PDF design. is_default=true makes it the account default (unsets others); is_archived hides it from pickers. Partial updates: only fields present are written.

tools.name: crm_estimate_update
tools.description: Update an editable estimate (status draft/sent/viewed/expired/declined). PATCHing an accepted/converted estimate returns 409 — duplicate it instead. Passing line_items replaces the full set.

tools.name: crm_forecast_weighted
tools.description: Probability-weighted forecast for open deals: SUM(value × stage_probability/100). Returns per-stage breakdown + grand total. Optional pipeline_id.

tools.name: crm_get_company
tools.description: Get a single CRM company by ID with its contacts, deals, and activities

tools.name: crm_get_contact
tools.description: Get a single CRM contact by ID, including their companies, deals, and activities

tools.name: crm_get_custom_field
tools.description: Read a single custom field definition by id.

tools.name: crm_get_custom_field_values
tools.description: Read all custom-field values on a contact/deal/company, keyed by field_key. Use to verify your custom-field writes landed before calling crm_enroll_sequence.

tools.name: crm_get_deal
tools.description: Get a single CRM deal by ID with pipeline, stage, contacts, companies, and activities

tools.name: crm_get_dnc_status
tools.description: Get the DNC (do-not-contact) status for a contact: email suppression, SMS opt-out, lifecycle state, and reasons. Check this before drafting outbound — sending to a DNC'd prospect is a compliance issue.

tools.name: crm_get_email_template
tools.description: Read a single template by id.

tools.name: crm_get_sequence
tools.description: Get a single sequence by id, including steps and current enrollment count.

tools.name: crm_get_user_signature
tools.description: Read a team member's HTML email signature. The full signature body — use when drafting sends from that user's connection.

tools.name: crm_ghl_contact_get
tools.description: Fetch one GHL contact with full custom fields, source, tags, owner.

tools.name: crm_ghl_contact_history
tools.description: Fetch a GHL contact's history: notes + tasks + conversations.

tools.name: crm_ghl_contacts_search
tools.description: Search GHL contacts. query is a free-text match.

tools.name: crm_ghl_opportunities_search
tools.description: Search GHL opportunities (= deals). Filter by pipeline_id, pipeline_stage_id, or contact_id.

tools.name: crm_ghl_pipelines_list
tools.description: List GHL pipelines (and their stages) for the connected location.

tools.name: crm_ghl_status
tools.description: GoHighLevel connection health (location id + name) or { connected: false } if not linked.

tools.name: crm_hubspot_contact_get
tools.description: Fetch one HubSpot contact with all properties.

tools.name: crm_hubspot_contact_history
tools.description: Fetch a HubSpot contact's history: notes + tasks (associated engagements).

tools.name: crm_hubspot_contacts_search
tools.description: Search HubSpot contacts.

tools.name: crm_hubspot_deals_search
tools.description: Search HubSpot deals.

tools.name: crm_hubspot_lists_list
tools.description: List HubSpot static + dynamic lists (for audience selection).

tools.name: crm_hubspot_pipelines_list
tools.description: List HubSpot deal pipelines + stages.

tools.name: crm_hubspot_status
tools.description: HubSpot connection health (portal id, timezone, currency) or { connected: false }.

tools.name: crm_import_preflight
tools.description: Dry-run a bulk import payload without writing anything. Returns a per-payload audit: invalid rows + reasons, intra-batch duplicates, cross-DB duplicates, unknown custom field keys (would_fail_on_unknown_fields=true if auto_create_fields is false). Run this BEFORE every bulk import call when migrating large datasets — surfaces problems at row 0 instead of row 3,000.

tools.name: crm_inbox_connections
tools.description: List all connected inboxes (Gmail / Outlook) for the account — id, email, platform, is_active.

tools.name: crm_inbox_list
tools.description: Return the last N messages from a connected inbox (no search). folder='inbox' | 'sent' | 'all'. Omit connection_id to use the account default.

tools.name: crm_inbox_recent
tools.description: Search a connected inbox with Gmail/Outlook native query syntax. Examples: 'from:logan@x.com newer_than:14d', 'subject:"intro call"', 'to:me has:attachment'. Use crm_inbox_list (no query) for the simple recent-N case.

tools.name: crm_integration_sync_configure
tools.description: Upsert a sync job. source='ghl'|'hubspot'. frequency_seconds clamped to [900, 86400]. plan_json defines the import shape (see crm_ghl_import_analyze / crm_hubspot_import_analyze).

tools.name: crm_integration_sync_disable
tools.description: Disable a sync job (keeps the row for audit). Re-enable via _configure with enabled=true.

tools.name: crm_integration_sync_list
tools.description: List configured external-CRM sync jobs (GHL / HubSpot → Hiveku) for the account.

tools.name: crm_integration_sync_run_now
tools.description: Trigger a sync to run on the next cron tick (zeros last_run_at).

tools.name: crm_invoice_template_create
tools.description: Create an invoice template. line_items is required (min 1). amount_cents is stamped server-side on each item. default_due_days seeds the invoice due date (issue_date + days).

tools.name: crm_invoice_template_delete
tools.description: Soft-delete an invoice template (deleted_at timestamp; not surfaced in list).

tools.name: crm_invoice_template_get
tools.description: Get a single invoice template by UUID.

tools.name: crm_invoice_template_list
tools.description: List reusable invoice templates (name, description, currency, default tax, net terms, line items skeleton).

tools.name: crm_invoice_template_update
tools.description: Update an invoice template. Passing line_items replaces the full set. Partial updates: only fields present are written.

tools.name: crm_lead_triage
tools.description: One-shot lead intake: inbox sweep + prospect parse + CRM dedupe + last-outbound lookup. Provider-agnostic (Typeform/JotForm/Webflow/Instantly/Lemlist/Smartlead/Calendly all work via the same query). Saved query patterns live in memory under domain='lead_intake_query'.

tools.name: crm_link_contact_company
tools.description: Link an existing contact to an existing company. When is_primary=true, the contact's previous primary company is demoted automatically.

tools.name: crm_link_deal_contact
tools.description: Link an existing contact to an existing deal. Idempotent.

tools.name: crm_list_activities
tools.description: List CRM activities (notes, calls, emails, meetings, tasks) with filters

tools.name: crm_list_companies
tools.description: List CRM companies with optional search and industry filter

tools.name: crm_list_contacts
tools.description: List CRM contacts with optional filtering by search term, lifecycle stage, company, with pagination

tools.name: crm_list_custom_fields
tools.description: List custom field DEFINITIONS for the account, optionally filtered by object_type. Returns field_key/label/field_type/options.

tools.name: crm_list_deals
tools.description: List CRM deals with filters for status, pipeline, stage, contact, company, and stale deals

tools.name: crm_list_email_connections
tools.description: List the account's active connected Gmail/Outlook inboxes. Returns id/user_id/email_address/platform. Use to find the connection_id when staging "send from" overrides on sequence enrollments.

tools.name: crm_list_email_suppressions
tools.description: List active email suppressions on the account. Optional ?email=... narrows to one address. Read-only — to ADD suppression use crm_set_dnc (atomic across multiple tables); this is for audit / visibility.

tools.name: crm_list_email_templates
tools.description: List the account's email templates (non-archived by default). Use to find a template_id before referencing it on a sequence step.

tools.name: crm_list_lead_source_options
tools.description: List the account's lead-source attribution options. Returns id/value/label/sort_order/is_default. Call before setting lead_source on a contact.

tools.name: crm_list_lead_status_options
tools.description: List the account's lead-status (operational sub-state within lead lifecycle) options. Returns id/value/label/color/sort_order/is_system. Call before crm_update_contact with a lead_status value.

tools.name: crm_list_pipelines
tools.description: List all CRM pipelines with their stages and deal counts

tools.name: crm_list_sequence_enrollments
tools.description: Paginated list of enrollments on a sequence with status filter. Use to find who's currently in a sequence vs exited/completed.

tools.name: crm_list_sequences
tools.description: List sales-sequence definitions (Cold Email 2, drip sequences, etc.) for the current account. Returns id, name, is_active, step count.

tools.name: crm_list_users
tools.description: List team members on the account (primary users + invited members). Returns id/clerk_user_id/name/email/avatar/has_signature. Use to find owner_id when assigning contacts/deals.

tools.name: crm_pause_sequence_enrollment
tools.description: Pause an active enrollment. The cron engine skips paused rows, but in-flight queue rows still dispatch on their normal tick.

tools.name: crm_pipeline_stage_summary
tools.description: Per-stage open-deal counts and $ totals for a pipeline. Default: first/oldest pipeline if pipeline_id omitted.

tools.name: crm_pipeline_velocity
tools.description: Approximate mean dwell time per stage (in days). Computed from stage_history JSON on each deal — best-effort, depends on stage-change paths populating that array.

tools.name: crm_reminder_cancel

tools.description: List PM projects (project_type filters: app_dev | website | seo | marketing | ppc).

tools.name: pm_sections_create

tools.name: pm_sections_delete

tools.name: pm_sections_list

tools.name: pm_sections_update

tools.name: pm_task_attachment_create

Goes to S3 under pm-tasks/<task_id>/... LINK — pass `file_url` (https://...) + optional link_title + link_description. No upload, just records the URL (e.g. Figma mockup, Loom recording, Google Doc). Works on subtasks too (just pass…

tools.name: pm_task_attachment_delete
tools.description: Remove an attachment from a PM task. For file uploads, also purges the S3 object (best-effort — DB row delete proceeds even if S3 fails). For link-style attachments, just deletes the DB row. Doesn't touch the task itself.

tools.name: pm_task_attachments_list
tools.description: List attachments on a PM task (or subtask — subtasks are pm_tasks with parent_task_id set, same endpoint). Returns id, attachment_type (image|video|audio|document|file|link), filename, file_url, file_size, mime_type, link_title/description, created_at.

tools.name: pm_task_claim
tools.description: Claim a PM task for an agent. Only tasks in status 'todo' or 'queued' can be claimed; anything else returns 409, as does a task another agent already holds. Atomically sets status to in_progress, stamps the agent codename, and mints branch olympus/task-<task_number>.

tools.name: pm_task_comments_list
tools.description: List a PM task's comment thread (oldest first). Each row: content, created_at, and the author as author_name/author_email (humans + review-link guests), agent_codename (agent-authored, null for humans), or user_id. parent_comment_id links threaded replies; attachments is an array of {name, url, type, size}. Companion read for pm_tasks_comment (which only appends). Accepts `id` or `task_id`.

tools.name: pm_task_dependencies_list
tools.description: Both directions of a PM task's dependencies: blocked_by (tasks that must finish first) and blocking (tasks waiting on this one), each with task_number, title, status, is_done and the dependency_id needed to remove the link. Also returns is_blocked_by_dependencies and open_blocker_count for the task itself. NOTE: a task can be blocked by dependencies without having status 'blocked' - the two are se…

tools.name: pm_task_dependency_create
tools.description: Record that a PM task cannot start until another one is done. Both tasks must be in the SAME project. Only finish_to_start is supported; start_to_start, finish_to_finish and start_to_finish are reserved and rejected, because PM has no gantt or scheduler to act on a date shift. Refuses self-links (400), duplicates (409) and any link that would close a cycle (409). Adding a dependency does NOT chang…

tools.name: pm_task_dependency_delete
tools.description: Remove ONE dependency link between two PM tasks. Deletes only the link; neither task is modified or deleted. Get dependency_id from pm_task_dependencies_list.

tools.name: pm_task_get_mc_link
tools.description: Reverse lookup: given a pm_task id, return the Mission Control card linked to it (if any). An agent working a pm_task uses this to pull the decision context — the original mc card body usually carries the WHY behind the work, plus the decision_answer if the human picked a structured option. Returns null in mc_task when nothing is linked. Surfaces multiple_linked: true + all_linked[] if (rarely) mo…

tools.name: pm_task_recurrence_create
tools.description: Create a recurring PM task template. On every cron match, the materializer spawns a NEW parent pm_task (status='queued') plus a child task for each entry in subtask_templates. Use this when work repeats on a cadence — weekly status reports, monthly billing, daily standup checklists, quarterly reviews. Cron is standard 5-field (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week). Examples: '0 9 * * 1' → ev…

tools.name: pm_task_recurrence_delete
tools.description: Delete a recurrence. Spawned tasks REMAIN (their recurrence_id is set to null) — only future cron fires are stopped. Use pm_task_recurrence_pause for a reversible stop.

tools.name: pm_task_recurrence_get
tools.description: Fetch one PM task recurrence by id.

tools.name: pm_task_recurrence_list
tools.description: List PM task recurrences for the account. Optionally filter by project_id or active_only=true. Returns each recurrence with its cron, timezone, last_fired_at, total_occurrences, on_overlap policy, and the parent + subtask templates.

tools.name: pm_task_recurrence_pause
tools.description: Pause a recurrence (is_active=false). Existing spawned tasks keep working; only future cron fires are suppressed. Idempotent — safe to call on an already-paused row.

tools.name: pm_task_recurrence_resume
tools.description: Resume a paused recurrence (is_active=true). The next cron match fires normally. Does NOT backfill occurrences missed while paused — call pm_task_recurrence_run_now after resume if you want a one-off catch-up. Idempotent.

tools.name: pm_task_recurrence_run_now
tools.description: Spawn one occurrence right now, off-schedule. Useful for testing a freshly-created recurrence, backfilling a missed fire after a worker outage, or kicking the loop while keeping the regular schedule. Respects on_overlap unless force=true is passed.

tools.name: pm_task_recurrence_update
tools.description: Update a recurrence. Any subset of fields can be patched; subtask_templates fully replaces the array when supplied (pass the complete intended set). Changing `cron` takes effect on the NEXT cron tick — already-fired occurrences are not retroactively rescheduled. Pausing? Prefer pm_task_recurrence_pause for the explicit semantics.

tools.name: pm_task_release
tools.description: Release a PM task an agent can no longer finish. Only 'in_progress' or 'blocked' tasks can be released. Resets status to queued, clears the agent codename and branch name, and zeroes progress.

tools.name: pm_task_submit_for_review
tools.description: Hand finished agent work to QA. Only 'in_progress' or 'qa' tasks are accepted. Sets status to qa, NOT done - use pm_tasks_complete for the human-final done state. It stamps completed_at even though the task is not complete, so judge completion by status and never by completed_at.

tools.name: pm_task_time_log_create
tools.description: Log time against a PM task. Requires EXACTLY ONE of user_id (a member of this account, for a human timesheet entry) or agent_codename (to record work an agent did) - never both, because the row records one actor and attributing agent hours to a person puts them on that person's billable timesheet. MONEY IS IN DOLLARS, not cents: hourly_rate 75 means $75/hr. total_cost is computed server-side. hour…

tools.name: pm_task_time_logs_list
tools.description: Time entries logged against a PM task: hours, date, description, billable flag, hourly rate and total cost, plus the rolled-up task_actual_hours and billable/total sums. Each entry says whether a person or an agent logged it. MONEY IS IN DOLLARS, not cents.

tools.name: pm_tasks_comment
tools.description: Add a comment to a PM task. Author codename defaults to 'olympus'. Accepts both `id` and `task_id` for the task identifier (older agent docs use task_id); accepts both `content` and `body` for the comment text.

tools.name: pm_tasks_complete
tools.description: Mark a PM task done. Sets status='done', completed_at=now, progress_percentage=100. Optional `summary` adds an audit comment on the task. Use pm_tasks_uncomplete to reverse.

tools.name: pm_tasks_create
tools.description: Create a PM task. task_number auto-increments per project. Field is `title` (NOT `name` — that's pm_projects_create). The route also accepts `name` as a forgiving alias if you forget.

tools.name: pm_tasks_create_bulk
tools.description: Bulk-create PM tasks (up to 500 per call). Each task must include project_id + title (or `name` as alias). task_number is auto-assigned per project. Validates ownership of every project_id before any insert — one bad project_id blocks the whole batch.

tools.name: pm_tasks_delete
tools.description: Delete a PM task.

tools.description: Fetch one PM task by UUID. tools.name: pm_tasks_list
tools.description: List PM tasks. Filter by project_id / status / assigned_to_id / parent_task_id (for subtasks) / section_id / milestone_id.

tools.name: pm_tasks_reassign_bulk
tools.description: Reassign many PM tasks at once (single updateMany — fast).

tools.name: pm_tasks_subtasks
tools.description: List subtasks of a parent task. Shorthand for pm_tasks_list with parent_task_id.

tools.name: pm_tasks_uncomplete
tools.description: Reopen a completed task. Clears completed_at, resets status (default 'in_progress'), resets progress_percentage (default 0). Use this instead of pm_tasks_update — the update PATCH allow-list doesn't include completed_at, so it can't fully undo a completion. Optional summary records a reopen comment on the task.

tools.name: pm_tasks_update
tools.description: Update a PM task — only the fields you pass are changed.

tools.name: ppc_account_settings_get
tools.description: Account-level settings — currency, time zone, auto-tagging, conversion-tracking status + id, customer name, manager/test-account flags, tracking_url_template, final_url_suffix. tools.name: ppc_ad_group_list
tools.description: List PPC ad groups. Filter by campaign_id / status.

tools.description: List PPC ads. Filter by ad_group_id / status.

tools.name: ppc_anomaly_check
tools.description: Compares yesterday's per-campaign cost / clicks / conversions vs the prior 7-day average. Use as a daily 'did anything blow up?' check — catches runaway spend, tracking breakage, sudden traffic drops. GOOGLE ADS ONLY. This tool routes to the Google Ads surface; passing a Microsoft/Meta/LinkedIn/TikTok conne…

tools.name: ppc_asset_attach
tools.description: Attach an existing asset to a campaign / ad_group / customer (account-wide). tools.name: ppc_asset_create
tools.description: Create an Asset (modern extensions API) at account level. Returns the asset's resource_name — use ppc_asset_attach to link to a campaign / ad_group / customer (account-wide). tools.name: ppc_asset_detach

tools.description: Auction Insights — who else competes in your auctions. Returns per-competitor-domain impression_share + overlap_rate + outranking_share + position_above_rate. Use to understand competitive pressure and identify domains worth monitoring. For low-impression-volume campaigns the report may be empty (Google requires sufficient volume).

tools.name: ppc_audience_attach

Audience resource_name is detected by…

Use to decide: keep & expand bid modifier (high conversions, low CPA), demote (high cost no conversions), or drop entirely. GOOGLE ADS ONLY. This tool routes to the Google Ads surface; passing a Microsoft/Meta/Li…

tools.name: ppc_bid_modifier_update

tools.name: ppc_bidding_strategy_update
tools.description: Switch a campaign's bidding strategy. tools.name: ppc_billing_summary
tools.description: Billing-setup snapshot — payments accounts linked, billing status, start/end dates. NOTE: detailed invoice/spend breakdowns aren't in the Ads API; this surfaces what's queryable. This tool routes to the Google Ads surface; passing a Microsoft/Meta/LinkedIn/TikTok connection_id returns a wrong-platf…

tools.name: ppc_bing_ad_extension_associate
tools.description: Attach existing Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) ad extensions (ids from the create lanes / ppc_bing_ad_extension_list) to a campaign or ad group (exactly one of campaign_id OR ad_group_id). THIS is the step that makes an extension serve. Max 20 per call. Needs prior ppc_sync.

tools.name: ppc_bing_ad_extension_list
tools.description: READ ad extensions on the Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) account. Default types SitelinkAdExtension + CalloutAdExtension; override with extension_types (comma-separated Microsoft type names). Max 100 per read (Microsoft's cap).

tools.name: ppc_bing_ad_schedule_add
tools.description: Dayparting on a Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) campaign or ad group (exactly one of campaign_id OR ad_group_id). schedules is an array of {day, from_hour (0-23), to_hour (0-24), from_minute?, to_minute? (0/15/30/45), bid_adjustment_percent?}. WARNING: adding ANY schedule restricts serving to the listed windows — unlisted hours STOP serving. Needs prior ppc_sync.

tools.name: ppc_bing_audience_associations_list
tools.description: READ every audience attached to one Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) campaign or ad group (exactly one of campaign_id OR ad_group_id), split targeted vs excluded, with the entity's audience_mode (bid_only vs target_and_bid — the only way to see an entity is serving ONLY to its audiences). Returns the criterion_ids that ppc_bing_audience_criterion_remove takes. Needs prior ppc_sync.

tools.name: ppc_bing_audience_criterion_add
tools.description: Associate an existing audience (id from ppc_bing_audience_list) with a Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) campaign or ad group (exactly one of campaign_id OR ad_group_id) — bid boost, or exclude=true. Whether targeting restricts reach depends on the entity's target-and-bid mode (Microsoft defaults to bid_only = reach unchanged) — check ppc_bing_audience_associations_list. Needs prior ppc_sync.

tools.name: ppc_bing_audience_criterion_remove
tools.description: Detach audience criteria (targeted OR excluded) from a Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) campaign or ad group by criterion_id (from ppc_bing_audience_associations_list; exactly one of campaign_id OR ad_group_id). Refuses any id that is not an AUDIENCE criterion — use ppc_bing_criterion_delete for geo/schedule/device/demographic. Removing an exclusion WIDENS reach. Needs prior ppc_sync.

tools.name: ppc_bing_audience_list
tools.description: READ every audience the Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) account can target (remarketing, in-market, custom, similar, customer lists...) with the audience_type that ppc_bing_audience_criterion_add requires. Audience CREATION/upload is deliberately not exposed (PII policy) — this reads what already exists.

tools.name: ppc_bing_audience_target_setting_set
tools.description: Switch a Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) campaign or ad group (exactly one of campaign_id OR ad_group_id) between bid_only (Microsoft's default — audiences adjust bids, reach unchanged; the SAFE fix for an accidentally narrowed entity) and target_and_bid (serves ONLY to its targeted audiences — reach collapses to their size). Exclusions are unaffected. Needs prior ppc_sync.

tools.name: ppc_bing_callout_extension_create
tools.description: Create callout extensions ('Free Estimates', '24/7 Service') on a Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) account: array of strings <=25 chars, max 20 per call. Created NOT serving — associate via ppc_bing_ad_extension_associate to show them.

tools.name: ppc_bing_conversion_goal_create

tools.name: ppc_bing_conversion_goal_list
tools.description: READ every conversion goal on the Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) account (type, status, tracking status, revenue settings, exclude-from-bidding).

tools.name: ppc_bing_conversion_tracking_status
tools.description: READ the Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) conversion-readiness diagnostic: UET tags + install state, conversion goals + recording state, ready_for_conversion_bidding flag, and a plain-language verdict. Run BEFORE switching any campaign to max_conversions/target_cpa/target_roas.

tools.name: ppc_bing_criterion_delete
tools.description: Remove Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) targeting criterions by id (from ppc_bing_criterions_list; exactly one of campaign_id OR ad_group_id) — the undo for the location/radius/schedule/device/demographic add lanes. tools.name: ppc_bing_criterions_list
tools.description: READ every targeting criterion (location, radius, location intent, ad schedule, device, age, gender) plus audience criterions on ONE Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) campaign or ad group (exactly one of campaign_id OR ad_group_id). tools.name: ppc_bing_demographic_criterion_add
tools.description: Age and/or gender bid adjustments on a Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) campaign or ad group (exactly one of campaign_id OR ad_group_id). age_ranges: 18-24 | 25-34 | 35-49 | 50-64 | 65+ | unknown; genders: male | female | unknown. At least one of the two. There is no exclude flag — Microsoft expresses a demographic exclusion as bid_adjustment_percent=-100. Needs prior ppc_sync.

tools.name: ppc_bing_device_criterion_set
tools.description: Set the bid adjustment for one device class (computers | smartphones | tablets) on a Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) campaign or ad group (exactly one of campaign_id OR ad_group_id). bid_adjustment_percent -100..900 is REQUIRED; -100 removes the device class entirely. Updates the auto-created Device criterion in place. Needs prior ppc_sync.

tools.name: ppc_bing_keyword_performance
tools.description: READ Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) keywords (id, text, match type, status, bid, editorial status) for one ad group, or for every locally-synced ad group when ad_group_id is omitted (run ppc_bing_pull_ad_groups first in that case). This is where Bing keyword_ids for ppc_platform_keyword_bid_update / ppc_platform_keyword_match_type_change come from — keywords are NOT mirrored locally.

tools.name: ppc_bing_location_criterion_add

tools.name: ppc_bing_location_intent_set

tools.name: ppc_bing_location_search
tools.description: READ. Resolve a place name or postal code ('Dallas', '75201', 'Texas') to Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) location ids for ppc_bing_location_criterion_add. Optional country_code (ISO) and location_types (comma-separated, e.g. 'City,PostalCode') filters.

tools.name: ppc_bing_radius_criterion_add

tools.name: ppc_bing_shared_negative_list_associate

tools.name: social_account_analytics
tools.description: Get daily account-level analytics rows (followers, reach, engagement rate) for ONE connected social account. Requires social_account_id from social_list_accounts. Paginated, newest day first.

tools.name: social_account_get
tools.description: One connected social account: platform, display name, follower count, granted scopes, capability flags and crucially connection_status plus last_error. Read this before blaming a publish failure on the post -- an expired or errored connection is the usual cause. Never returns tokens.

tools.name: social_analytics_best_times
tools.description: Suggested posting times computed from THIS account's own engagement history, returned as concrete future timestamps ready to pass as scheduled_at. Returns an empty list on a new account or one with too few samples: that is the honest answer, not a failure, and means schedule by the calendar instead.

tools.name: social_analytics_followers
tools.description: Follower growth per connected account over `period` days, with a daily series and a rolled-up summary of gained, lost and net change. Reads STORED snapshots, so an account whose last_synced_at is old reports stale growth rather than an error -- check last_synced_at before reading a flat line as a flat audience.

tools.name: social_analytics_summary
tools.description: Get social media analytics summary — total posts, engagement, reach across all platforms

tools.name: social_analytics_sync
tools.description: Refresh post analytics for this account from the platforms, capped at 50 post versions, and return the run report. It only refreshes posts that are DUE, so calling it twice reports zero synced the second time -- that is correct, not a failure. To force one specific post use social_post_sync_analytics.

tools.name: social_analytics_timeseries
tools.description: Get daily social analytics time series across the account: engagement deltas, follower growth, top posts, best-time heatmap, and per-platform totals. NOTE: the backing builder route ships in a later deploy — until then this returns 404; metrics appear once analytics sync is enabled for the account.

tools.name: social_calendar_create
tools.description: Create a social calendar event. Can link to an existing post (linked_post_id) or campaign (linked_campaign_id).

tools.name: social_calendar_delete
tools.description: Delete a social calendar event by ID.

tools.name: social_calendar_get
tools.description: Get one social calendar event with its linked post and content pillar. Use after social_calendar_list to see what a slot actually holds before rescheduling it.

tools.name: social_calendar_list
tools.description: List social calendar events (planned posts, campaigns, holidays) with optional date-range, event-type, and status filters. Paginated, ordered by start date.

tools.name: social_calendar_update
tools.description: Update a social calendar event — title, dates, type, status, recurrence, links, tags, or platforms. Only provided fields are changed.

tools.name: social_comment_get
tools.description: Get one comment from the engagement inbox with its post, the connected account it arrived on, our own reply if any, and any threaded replies. reply_content plus replied_at is the record that a reply was actually published; a comment with neither is unanswered.

tools.name: social_comment_reply
tools.description: PUBLISHES A PUBLIC REPLY to a comment on Facebook, Instagram or LinkedIn, then records it against the inbox row. Outward-facing and immediate: there is no draft mode and no undo. The platform call happens first, so a failure means nothing was posted AND nothing was recorded. A response with recorded:false means the reply IS live but the local write failed -- re-read the comment, never retry, becau…

tools.name: social_comment_update
tools.description: TRIAGE ONLY -- nothing here reaches the platform. Sets workflow state on a comment: status, sentiment, requires_response, ai_category, and ai_suggested_response (a DRAFT reply, stored and never sent). To actually publish a reply call social_comment_reply. Passing reply_content here is rejected with 400: it used to be accepted, recorded as sent, and posted nowhere.

tools.name: social_comments_list
tools.description: List social comments received across all published posts, with status, sentiment, requires-response, and text-search filters. READ-ONLY for now — replying to comments via this surface is not yet supported; reply/dismiss actions live in the dashboard.

tools.name: social_create_post
tools.description: Create a new social media post targeting specific platforms and accounts

tools.name: social_delete_post
tools.description: Delete a social media post by ID

tools.name: social_get_post
tools.description: Get a single social media post by ID with versions and analytics

tools.name: social_hashtag_get
tools.description: Get one tracked hashtag with its stored usage and performance counters. Returns what has been recorded for it, not live platform volume.

tools.name: social_hashtag_update
tools.description: Update a tracked hashtag's classification flags. The route accepts exactly four fields -- category, is_branded, is_favorite, is_trending -- and silently ignores anything else, so the tag TEXT cannot be edited here: delete the row and create it again.

tools.name: social_hashtags_create
tools.description: Register a hashtag for tracking on a platform. Upserts — calling again for the same hashtag+platform updates category/flags instead of duplicating. A leading "#" is added if missing.

tools.name: social_hashtags_delete
tools.description: Delete a tracked hashtag by ID (from social_hashtags_list).

tools.name: social_hashtags_list
tools.description: List tracked hashtags with performance metrics (times used, avg engagement, avg reach). Filter by platform, trending/branded/favorite flags; sort by engagement, used, reach, or trending rank.

tools.name: social_linkedin_comment_add
tools.description: PUBLISHES A PUBLIC TOP-LEVEL COMMENT on a LinkedIn post as the connected page or profile, immediately. Outward-facing, no draft mode, no undo. This is for commenting on someone else's post; to answer a comment on our own post use social_comment_reply, which records the reply against the engagement inbox so it is not re-surfaced as unanswered.

tools.name: social_linkedin_comment_delete
tools.description: PERMANENTLY DELETES A COMMENT FROM LINKEDIN. Destructive, outward-facing and irreversible: LinkedIn keeps no copy and offers no restore. It can remove someone else's comment from a page you administer, so treat it as moderation and confirm with a human first. Deleting a comment does NOT remove the stored row in the engagement inbox.

tools.name: social_linkedin_comment_list
tools.description: LIVE comment thread on ANY LinkedIn post URN the connection can see, including posts Hiveku never published. The engagement inbox only covers our own posts and only refreshes every 2 hours. For a post Hiveku did publish, prefer social_post_comments_sync -- it stores what it finds so replies can be tracked.

tools.name: social_linkedin_follower_stats
tools.description: LIVE organization follower composition: organic vs paid, broken down by association type (employee, member) and by job function. This is WHO follows the page, not a follower count over time -- for the trend use social_analytics_followers. Breakdown arrays come back null when LinkedIn withholds them below its minimum audience size, which is not an error. ORGANIZATION CONNECTIONS ONLY.

tools.name: social_linkedin_member_stats
tools.description: LIVE creator analytics for a PERSONAL LinkedIn profile: impressions, likes, comments, shares, clicks and engagement rate per post, plus the follower count. The organization endpoints refuse personal connections, so this is their only analytics surface. Pass post_urn to scope to one post. Needs the member analytics scopes on the LinkedIn app; an app without them returns 502 however the connection w…

tools.name: social_linkedin_organization_get
tools.description: LIVE LinkedIn organization detail: name, vanity name, description, website, logo and follower count. org_id is the bare numeric id (1234567), not a URN. Returns 502 when this connection does not administer that organization -- LinkedIn refuses the read rather than returning an empty record.

tools.name: social_linkedin_organization_list
tools.description: LIVE from LinkedIn: the organizations this connection administers, with the ACL role granting it. This is what LinkedIn believes now, not what social_accounts has stored -- use it to find the organization id of a page that is not connected yet, or to confirm an admin was not removed from the page behind our back. A personal-profile connection returns an empty list, not an error.

tools.name: social_linkedin_page_stats
tools.description: LIVE organization PAGE traffic: page views split by tab (all, overview, careers) and unique visitors. This is profile traffic, NOT post reach -- someone who saw a post in the feed is not counted here. ORGANIZATION CONNECTIONS ONLY. Supply from_date and to_date together for a per-day range.

tools.name: social_linkedin_post_list
tools.description: The connected page's or profile's ACTUAL LinkedIn timeline, read live. social_list_posts only knows about posts Hiveku published; this is the only way to see posts made on LinkedIn directly. Returns the post URN, which is what the reactions, comments and member-analytics tools take. limit caps at 50 (LinkedIn's own maximum); page with start.

tools.name: social_linkedin_profile_get
tools.description: LIVE LinkedIn profile of the MEMBER who authorized this connection, even when it posts as an organization page -- the token always belongs to a person. Use it to confirm a token is still live and whose consent it carries.

tools.name: social_linkedin_reaction_add
tools.description: PUBLISHES A PUBLIC REACTION on a LinkedIn post as the connected page or profile, immediately. Outward-facing, and this route offers no undo. Use it to engage from the brand account on a partner or employee post, not on your own content.

tools.name: social_linkedin_reaction_list
tools.description: LIVE reaction counts on a post broken down by type (LIKE, CELEBRATE, SUPPORT, LOVE, INSIGHTFUL, FUNNY). The stored analytics snapshot flattens all of these into one like count, so this is the only way to see that a post got INSIGHTFUL rather than LIKE. An older post whose reactions LinkedIn no longer serves returns an empty object, not an error.

tools.name: social_linkedin_share_stats
tools.description: LIVE organization share statistics: impressions, unique impressions, clicks, likes, comments, shares and engagement for the page as a whole, with organic-only figures alongside the totals so paid amplification does not read as organic reach. ORGANIZATION CONNECTIONS ONLY -- a personal profile returns 400, use social_linkedin_member_stats. Supply from_date and to_date TOGETHER for a per-day breakdo…

tools.name: social_list_accounts
tools.description: List connected social media accounts with optional platform and status filters

tools.name: social_list_posts
tools.description: List social media posts with filters for status, platform, content type, date range, and AI generation flag

tools.name: social_meta_post_list
tools.description: The connected Facebook Page's or Instagram account's ACTUAL feed, read live from the Graph API. social_list_posts only knows what Hiveku published; this shows everything on the profile, including posts made in the Meta apps. tools.name: social_pillar_create
tools.description: Create a social content pillar — a recurring content theme with posting targets, example topics, hashtags, and guidelines.

tools.name: social_pillar_delete
tools.description: Delete a content pillar. Posts assigned to it are unlinked (pillar_id set to null), not deleted.

tools.name: social_pillar_get
tools.description: Get one content pillar with its targets, example topics, hashtags and guidelines. Read it before drafting so a post lands on the theme the account actually committed to.

tools.name: social_pillar_list
tools.description: List social content pillars (recurring content themes the account posts about) with per-pillar post counts, ordered by sort order.

tools.name: social_pillar_update
tools.description: Update a content pillar — name, targets, topics, hashtags, guidelines, active flag, or sort order. Only provided fields are changed.

tools.name: social_post_analytics
tools.description: Get per-post metrics for one social post: aggregated totals (impressions, reach, engagements, likes, comments, shares, saves, clicks, video views, engagement rate) plus a per-platform-version breakdown with each version's platform URL, account, and latest analytics snapshot.

tools.name: social_post_comments_sync
tools.description: Pull a post's comments from its platforms RIGHT NOW and return them, including the ones just ingested. The engagement inbox only refreshes every 2 hours, so call this before replying or the thread will be stale. Covers Facebook, Instagram and LinkedIn; platforms with no comment API return the stored rows with sync.synced 0 rather than an error. A resync never clobbers reply or triage fields.

tools.name: social_post_reject
tools.description: Reject a post that is HELD for approval: returns it to draft with approval_status 'rejected' and records the reason. Safe and reversible -- the post can be edited and staged again. There is deliberately no matching approve tool: releasing a held post is a human decision, made in the dashboard appro…

tools.name: social_post_sync_analytics
tools.description: Pull fresh engagement metrics for a post from the platform's API.

tools.name: social_provider_list
tools.description: Every social platform Hiveku can connect, each with its OAuth redirect URI, required scopes, setup guide, and hiveku_native telling you whether a Hiveku app is configured on this deployment (false means the customer must register their own app). Read this before telling someone a platform is unsupported: usually the platform is fine and only the native app is unconfigured.

tools.name: social_publish_post
tools.description: Publish a social media post to the post's configured target accounts. GOVERNANCE GATE: publishing requires the post to be approved in the dashboard first. tools.name: social_schedule_slot_create
tools.description: Create a recurring posting slot. tools.name: social_schedule_slot_delete
tools.description: Delete a recurring posting slot. Posts already scheduled at that time KEEP their scheduled_at and still publish -- deleting a slot only stops it being offered in future. To stop a post, unschedule the post.

tools.name: social_schedule_slot_list
tools.description: List the account's recurring posting slots (weekday + minute of day + IANA timezone). A slot with social_account_id null applies to every connection; one with it set applies only to that connection. Slots describe WHEN the account wants to post; they do not schedule anything themselves.

tools.name: social_schedule_slot_next_open
tools.description: Next OPEN slot occurrences over a 14-day horizon: defined slots with no post already scheduled into them. Call this before scheduling instead of picking a time and hoping it is free. Returns an empty list when the account has defined no slots -- that is not an error, it means schedule by hand.

tools.name: social_schedule_slot_update
tools.description: Update a recurring posting slot. Only supplied fields change. Setting social_account_id to null widens the slot back to every connection. Returns 404 for a slot id that is not this account.

tools.name: social_update_post
tools.description: Update a social post's editable content: title, body, target platforms and schedule. It CANNOT change status or approval state. tools.name: stock_photos_download
tools.description: Fetch a stock-photo URL and save it to a project's assets (S3 + builder_project_assets row). save_path is the file path inside the project (e.g. 'public/images/hero.jpg').

tools.name: stock_photos_pixabay_search

tools.name: stock_photos_search
tools.description: Search Unsplash + Pexels for free stock photos. Returns merged results with { url, thumbnail, photographer, source, attribution }. Use the url with stock_photos_download to save into a project.

tools.name: supabase_auth_config_get
tools.description: Fetch the project's Supabase Auth config (signup, email confirmation, JWT, password policy, OAuth flags). tools.name: supabase_auth_config_update
tools.description: Update arbitrary Supabase auth config fields. config is the Management API PATCH body. NOTE on smtp_pass: in every response it appears as Supabase's ENCRYPTED stored form (a 64-hex blob). It never matches the literal password, its not-changing is NOT evidence the write failed or was substituted, and it must never be fed back as a password. To change it, send the new literal value; the echo will st…

tools.name: supabase_auth_user_create
tools.description: Admin-create a Supabase Auth user. Provide email OR phone (one required). password optional — if omitted, user must use a magic-link / OAuth flow to sign in. email_confirm / phone_confirm default true (skip the verification email). user_metadata is user-editable; app_metadata is admin-only and shows up in JWTs.

tools.name: supabase_auth_user_delete
tools.description: Delete an Auth user by UUID. Cascades to RLS-owned rows depending on FK config. Irreversible.

tools.name: supabase_auth_user_generate_link
tools.description: Generate an auth action link (magic link, password recovery, invite, email-change confirmation). type values: 'signup' | 'magiclink' | 'recovery' | 'invite' | 'email_change_current' | 'email_change_new'. Returns the action URL. Useful when you want to email the link yourself instead of letting Supabase send the templated email.

tools.name: supabase_auth_user_get
tools.description: Read one Auth user by UUID. The user_id is the value of auth.users.id (a UUID), NOT the email.

tools.name: supabase_auth_user_update
tools.description: Update one Auth user. Any of: email, phone, password, user_metadata, app_metadata, role, ban_duration. Set ban_duration='24h' / 'none' to ban/unban.

tools.name: supabase_auth_users_list
tools.description: List Supabase Auth users for the project (paginated). These are the END-USERS of the project's app — NOT Hiveku account members. Returns email, phone, created_at, last_sign_in_at, banned_until, and the user_metadata / app_metadata blobs.

tools.name: supabase_configure_hiveku_smtp
tools.description: Convenience: point Supabase Auth emails at Hiveku Email infra (SES + verified sender). Only sender_email needed.

tools.name: supabase_configure_oauth
tools.description: Enable/disable a Supabase OAuth provider with client_id + client_secret (github, google, apple, etc.).

tools.name: supabase_configure_smtp
tools.description: Point Supabase Auth emails (confirmation, magic links, password reset) at a custom SMTP server.

tools.name: supabase_edge_functions_delete
tools.description: Delete an edge function by slug.

tools.name: supabase_edge_functions_deploy
tools.description: Deploy one or more edge functions. functions is an array of { slug, source, import_map?, verify_jwt? }.

tools.name: supabase_edge_functions_get_source
tools.description: Fetch the source bundle for one edge function by slug.

tools.name: supabase_edge_functions_invoke
tools.description: Invoke an edge function. payload is JSON sent as the request body.

tools.name: supabase_edge_functions_list
tools.description: List edge functions deployed on the project.

tools.name: supabase_edge_functions_set_secrets
tools.description: Set project-level secrets visible to edge functions. secrets is a {KEY: value} map (strings only).

tools.name: supabase_gen_types
tools.description: Generate TypeScript types for the project's database schema. Returns a `types` string ready to drop into the project as e.g. lib/database.types.ts.

tools.name: supabase_migration_apply
tools.description: Apply a database migration. name is a short identifier (e.g. "add_user_preferences"), query is the full SQL. Migrations are recorded in Supabase's migration history so you can roll forward predictably. For ad-hoc/exploratory writes use database_execute instead.

tools.name: supabase_migrations_list
tools.description: List applied database migrations on the project.

tools.name: supabase_policies_list
tools.description: List Row-Level Security policies on the project DB via pg_policies. Pass `schema` and/or `table` to scope. Returns {schemaname, tablename, policyname, permissive, roles, cmd, qual, with_check}. Call this BEFORE policy_create to confirm whether a policy with the same name already exists on the target table.

tools.name: supabase_policy_create
tools.description: Create a new RLS policy via CREATE POLICY SQL on the project's Postgres. command is SELECT|INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE|ALL. roles is the list of pg roles (default ['authenticated']). `using` is the USING expression (read predicate); `check` is the WITH CHECK expression (write predicate). For SELECT use `using`; for INSERT use `check`; for UPDATE/DELETE you usually need both. schema, table, and each role …

tools.name: supabase_policy_delete
tools.description: Drop an RLS policy by name + table via DROP POLICY IF EXISTS. Irreversible. No-op (success) if the policy doesn't exist.

tools.name: supabase_policy_update
tools.description: Replace an existing RLS policy. Postgres only allows partial ALTER POLICY changes — to give you a clean "update everything" surface, this runs DROP+CREATE inside a single transaction. Pass `name` + `table` to identify the existing policy and the new field values as you would in policy_create. Use `new_name` to rename.

tools.name: supabase_storage_create
tools.description: Create a Storage bucket. is_public=true makes objects readable without auth. The bucket-name param is `bucket` (not `bucket_name`).

tools.name: supabase_storage_delete
tools.description: Delete an EMPTY Storage bucket (call supabase_storage_empty first if there are objects). The bucket-name param is `bucket` (not `bucket_name`).

tools.name: supabase_storage_empty
tools.description: Delete all objects in a Storage bucket (bucket itself stays).

tools.name: supabase_storage_list
tools.description: List Supabase Storage buckets for the project.

tools.name: supabase_storage_object_copy
tools.description: Copy an object to a new path inside the same bucket.

tools.name: supabase_storage_object_delete
tools.description: Delete a single object from a Supabase bucket. Permanent — no recycle bin.

tools.name: supabase_storage_object_download
tools.description: Download an object from a Supabase bucket. Returns {bucket, path, mime_type, file_size_bytes, content: <base64>, encoding}. Use for read-back smoke tests, content inspection, etc. Not the primary serve path — public buckets should be linked directly.

tools.name: supabase_storage_object_move
tools.description: Move/rename an object inside the same bucket. from + to are the object keys (paths inside the bucket).

tools.name: supabase_storage_object_signed_url
tools.description: Create a time-limited signed URL for a private bucket object. Default expires_in is 3600s (1h); max 7 days.

tools.name: supabase_storage_object_upload
tools.description: Upload a file to a Supabase Storage bucket. content is base64-encoded bytes (data:URI prefix accepted and stripped). Set upsert=true to overwrite an existing object at the same path. 25MB cap through MCP — use multipart uploads for larger files.

tools.name: supabase_storage_objects_list
tools.description: List files inside a Supabase Storage bucket (paginated). Use this in file-manager apps to enumerate the user's files. Pair with the bucket tools (supabase_storage_list/create) when you need to manage buckets themselves.

tools.name: supabase_sync_redirect_urls
tools.description: Set Supabase site_url + URI allow-list. Call after deploying so OAuth redirects + magic-link emails work.

tools.name: supabase_table_row_delete
tools.description: Delete rows matching filters. UNFILTERED DELETE IS REFUSED — always pass at least one filter. Returns the deleted rows.

tools.name: supabase_table_row_insert
tools.description: Insert one or more rows. `rows` may be a single object or an array of objects. Returns the inserted rows (representation).

tools.name: supabase_table_row_update
tools.description: Update rows matching filters. filters and patch are both required. filters={pk: value} for a single-row update.

tools.name: supabase_table_rows_list
tools.description: Read rows from a table via PostgREST. Safer than database_query for simple ops — no SQL injection surface, structured response. Use filters={col: value} for eq matches; for more complex predicates, fall back to database_query.

tools.name: survey_create
tools.description: Create a DRAFT survey. Omit `questions` to get the canonical starter set for the type — for nps and csat that is the standard wording, and changing it breaks comparability of the score, so prefer the default unless the user asked for something specific. Creating does not send anything: the survey lands in draft. Activate it with survey_update({status:"active"}), which requires at least one active …

tools.name: survey_get
tools.description: Get one survey with its active questions.

tools.name: survey_list
tools.description: List the account's surveys with rollups (delivery counts, response counts, and the headline NPS/CSAT metric). Start here to find a survey_id.

tools.name: survey_results
tools.description: Aggregate results: delivery funnel, the NPS/CSAT metric, bucket breakdown, and the latest completed responses INCLUDING free-text answers — use those verbatim quotes as real customer language for copy rather than inventing testimonials.

tools.name: survey_send
tools.description: SENDS THE SURVEY FOR REAL to the named recipients (email or SMS). Not a preview — confirm with the user before calling. Supply contact_ids (from the crm_* tools) and/or raw emails. Applies the same guards as a dashboard send: the survey must be active, the throttle window is enforced, duplicates are deduped, SMS respects quiet hours, and a single call is capped at 200 recipients. channel defaults …

tools.name: survey_update
tools.description: Update a survey: rename, activate/pause, adjust the re-ask throttle, or edit the delivery copy. Setting status="active" is what makes a survey sendable and REQUIRES at least one active question — it 400s otherwise. throttle_days is the re-contact guard: a contact surveyed within that window is skipped by survey_send rather than surveyed again.
